direction.question: When do explicit intervention and counterfactual structures improve learned-world planning under distribution shift relative to equally capable noncausal world models?
direction.closureCriteria: On held-out interventions and mechanism changes, a causal world model improves planning success, calibration, and sample efficiency over matched latent-dynamics and invariant-learning baselines, with gains surviving misspecified graphs and latent confounding.
partialResults: Causal World Models use unsupervised deconfounding and report improvements in reinforcement-learning sample complexity and counterfactual physical reasoning.
CausalVerse provides high-fidelity configurable simulations with known causal structure and intervention histories.
Existing causal-control systems remain mainly simulated or sensitive to structural assumptions.
starters: Individual: Reproduce a causal-world-model result in CausalWorld and add hidden-confounder, mechanism-shift, and graph-misspecification stress tests.
Small lab: Compare explicit causal, invariant, and standard latent world models on matched CausalVerse training data and unseen intervention families.
Well-funded lab: Collect controlled real-robot interventions and test whether simulation-learned causal structure improves adaptation to altered objects, actuators, and dynamics.

noveltyReview.scope: arXiv and official repositories for causal world models, causal representation learning, interventions, counterfactual physical reasoning, and causal reinforcement learning.
noveltyReview.note: Partial fusion already exists, so the open question concerns robust benefit and scaling rather than whether any causal world-model system exists.

counterexamples: Causal World Models explicitly combine learned dynamics, latent deconfounding, counterfactual prediction, and reinforcement learning.
Explainable reinforcement learning via causal world models combines causal structure with control and explanation.
Interventional causal-representation methods learn structure from intervention families in controlled settings.

direction.question: Under equal tuning and total-cost budgets, which data regimes and distribution shifts reliably favor neural or tabular-foundation models over boosted trees, and which still favor trees?
direction.closureCriteria: Produce a leak-checked, preregistered regime map covering IID, temporal, grouped, large, high-dimensional, missing, and high-cardinality data, with equal tuning time and total compute plus latency, calibration, and energy reporting.
partialResults: The earlier 45-dataset benchmark found tree-based models strongest on roughly 10,000-sample datasets.
TabArena finds deep methods catch up with larger time budgets and ensembles while foundation models excel on smaller datasets.
BeyondArena finds tabular foundation models strongest on tiny-to-medium IID data while trees and conventional deep models dominate several non-IID, large, and high-dimensional regimes.
starters: Individual: Compare CatBoost, XGBoost, TabPFN, and TabM on 8-12 datasets using both random and temporal splits under an identical one-hour tuning budget.
Small lab: Build a preregistered 100-plus-dataset regime map including latency, energy, calibration, missingness, high-cardinality features, and temporal or group shift.
Well-funded lab: Train a tabular foundation model on disjoint source corpora and evaluate frozen cross-domain and non-IID transfer against the best trees and AutoGluon under total-cost parity.

noveltyReview.scope: arXiv, living benchmarks, and official repositories for tabular deep learning, foundation models, gradient-boosted trees, temporal and group shift, and equal-budget comparisons.
noveltyReview.note: The old blanket claim that trees beat deep learning is no longer supportable; confidence is high only for the revised regime-selection and non-IID robustness question.

counterexamples: TabR beats gradient-boosted decision trees on a benchmark designed to be favorable to them.
TabPFN and later versions lead on several small-to-medium IID suites.
TabArena shows deep ensembles catch up under larger time budgets.
BeyondArena shows that no one family dominates across IID and non-IID regimes.
